pairs.question: Non omnis quaestio per numeros suos implenda est?
pairs.answer: Quidni? sed tamquam accessio, non tamquam summa.
pairs.derivation: Seneca quotes an imagined objector ('quid ergo? non omnis quaestio per numeros suos implenda est?') and answers it himself. Dropped the framing opener 'quid ergo?' (the interlocutor's lead-in) and normalized capitalization; the interrogative itself is kept contiguous. Answer is Seneca's own reply 'quidni? sed tamquam accessio, non tamquam summa.', ending at the full stop; what follows ('nullum habile membrum est, si corpori par est.') is a separate illustrative maxim, not part of the answer, so it was cut.

pairs.question: Apud quem praetorem causam dixisti?
pairs.derivation: From Varius Geminus's reported interrogation of the brother. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'interrogavi fratrem:' before the question and 'inquit' after the answer; normalized capitalization. Took only the first clean exchange of the chain; the subsequent questions ('quis accusator fuit?', 'quis testis...?') are interrupted by Seneca's authorial parenthesis '(uni enim etiam de minore scelere non creditur)' and form separate exchanges, so they were not stitched in.
